title.topic:
Joseph: Speaking Boldly
and by Faith
title.point: Even when things seem hopeless, we can speak boldly and by faith, trusting that God is in control and His plans will come true.

lyricsLeft.text: 1. Go! Stand and speak in the temple,
and speak to the people the Words of this life!
Go! Stand and speak in the temple,
and speak to the people the Words of this life!
God has exalted our Jesus and
made Him the Leader and Savior of men!
God has exalted our Jesus and
made Him the Leader and Savior of men!

lyricsRight.text: 2. We cannot be silent! But we have to speak
The things which we have seen,
The things which we have heard.
3. In and out of prison, but never stop your speaking;
Rejoicing to be worthy to suffer for this Name.
4. Speak and do not be afraid; I Myself am with you.
Here in this city I have many people — Speak! Do not be silent.
5. Go, stand and speak! Go, stand and speak!
Speak all the words, words of this life.
Oh, don't let anyone or anything stop you;
Go speak the words, words of this life.

lastWeekReview.title: Joseph: Cared For by God
bullets: Joseph's brothers plotted against him out of jealousy — they threw him into a pit and sold him to traders heading to Egypt.
Even after being sold as a slave, God was with Joseph. He worked faithfully for Potiphar, an Egyptian official.
God caused everything Joseph did to prosper, and Potiphar noticed — he put Joseph in charge of his entire household.
Joseph didn't become bitter or give up hope — he trusted God's plan even when life seemed unfair.
God cared for Joseph through every trial, showing that He is faithful even in our darkest moments.
lastWeekReview.discussion: 📖  When something unfair happens to you, how can you still trust that God has a plan?
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God." — Romans 8:28

kidsContent.text: Remember how Joseph was working for Potiphar in Egypt and everything was going great? Well, something terrible happened. Potiphar's wife told a big lie about Joseph — she accused him of something he never did! Potiphar was so angry that he had Joseph thrown into prison.

Imagine being punished for something you didn't do! Most people would be super upset and give up. But Joseph was different. He didn't stop believing in the special dreams God had given him. He knew that God's plans are bigger than any problem.
Even in prison, God was with Joseph! The chief jailer saw something special in Joseph and put him in charge of all the other prisoners. God's care never stopped, even behind bars.
💡 Sometimes bad things happen to good people, but God never leaves us — He is always working behind the scenes!
Speaking Boldly by Faith — The Dreams Interpreted
One morning, Joseph noticed two prisoners looking very worried — the royal cupbearer and the royal baker. They had both had mysterious dreams and didn't know what they meant.

Here's the amazing part: Joseph's OWN dreams from God hadn't come true yet! He was still stuck in prison. But did Joseph say, "Forget about dreams, they don't come true"? NO! Instead, he spoke boldly: "Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams!"
That's what it means to speak BY FAITH — speaking based on what you believe God can do, not based on what you see right now.

Joseph told the cupbearer: "In three days, you'll be free and serve Pharaoh again!" Three days later, everything happened EXACTLY as Joseph said! His bold faith-speaking is what eventually got him out of prison!
🌟 We can be like Joseph! Even when things are hard, we can speak boldly about what God can do!

pages.practicePoint: This week, when you feel discouraged or unsure, try to speak something bold about God — like telling a friend "God has a plan!" — and be ready to share your story next week!

memoryVerse.text: "All things are possible to him who believes."
memoryVerse.application: Just like Joseph believed God's dreams would come true — even when he was stuck in prison — we can believe that ALL things are possible when we trust in God!

activity.title: Dream Interpreter Challenge
activity.format: Role Play + Guessing Game + Verse Practice
activity.materials: Printed role play scripts, small cards with "dream clues", whiteboard/markers, memory verse strips

parts.name: Part 1 — Role Play: Joseph in Prison (8 min)
parts.description: Assign roles: Joseph, Cupbearer, Baker, Narrator, Prison Guard. Read through the script together. Joseph speaks boldly when the prisoners share their dreams. Emphasize HOW Joseph spoke — with confidence in God, not in himself.

parts.name: Part 2 — Dream Clue Guessing Game (5 min)
parts.description: Prepare cards with picture clues (grapes, cup, basket, birds, number 3). Kids take turns drawing a card and guessing which dream it belongs to — cupbearer or baker? Discuss: "How did Joseph know the answers? (God told him!)"

parts.name: Part 3 — Verse Relay (5 min)
parts.description: Write Mark 9:23 on strips (one word per strip). Split into teams. Each team races to arrange the verse in order. First team done reads it aloud boldly — just like Joseph spoke boldly! Repeat 2-3 times.

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: A dark prison in Egypt. Joseph is helping organize things. The Cupbearer and Baker sit looking worried.
One morning, Joseph noticed two prisoners looking very sad and troubled.
Hey, why do you both look so sad today? What's wrong?
We both had strange dreams last night, and nobody can tell us what they mean!
Yeah, it's really bothering us. We don't understand our dreams at all.
Joseph stands up straight and speaks with confidence.
Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams — God can show us what they mean!
The Cupbearer leans forward eagerly.
In my dream, I saw a vine with three branches. The branches budded, blossomed, and grew grapes! I squeezed the grapes into Pharaoh's cup and gave it to him.
This is what your dream means: The three branches are three days. In three days, Pharaoh will bring you out of prison and you'll be his cupbearer again!
Really?! That's wonderful!
When you get out, please remember me. I was brought here from the land of the Hebrews, and I've done nothing wrong. Please mention me to Pharaoh so I can be set free!
I will, Joseph! I promise I'll remember you!
My dream was about three baskets of white bread on my head. The top basket was full of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds kept eating from it!
Joseph pauses, then speaks carefully.
The three baskets also mean three days. But… within three days, Pharaoh will sentence you to die. I'm sorry.
(gasps) Oh no…
Three days later, everything happened exactly as Joseph said. The cupbearer went back to serve Pharaoh. But the cupbearer forgot all about Joseph. Joseph stayed in prison for two more years!
(sitting alone, praying) God, I believe You are with me. Even though I'm still here, I trust Your plan.
Two years later, Pharaoh himself had a mysterious dream. The cupbearer finally remembered Joseph!
Joseph, I heard you can interpret dreams. Can you tell me what mine means?
It is not in me. God will give Pharaoh a favorable answer!
All kids together:
Let's be like Joseph — ones who speak boldly by faith!

description.text: Setup: Two relay lanes. At the end of each lane, place a basket with picture cards (grapes, cup, bread, birds, vine, Pharaoh). Each card has "Cupbearer" or "Baker" written on the back.

Rules: First runner sprints to the basket, grabs a card, shouts which dream it belongs to — "CUPBEARER!" or "BAKER!" — then flips to check. If correct, run back and tag the next. If wrong, do 3 jumping jacks first.
Materials: Picture cards (10+ per team), 2 baskets, cones for relay lanes
📖 Connection: Just like Joseph quickly and boldly interpreted dreams, kids must quickly identify which dream each clue belongs to!
Setup: Open gym space. Choose 2 taggers ("Potiphar's Guards"). Everyone else is a "prisoner" trying to avoid being tagged.
Rules: When tagged, you're "frozen in prison" (arms crossed). To be freed, another player comes to you and you both say together: "All things are possible to him who believes!" Then both are free.
📖 Connection: Just like Joseph was stuck in prison but spoke boldly by faith to get free, kids must speak the memory verse to free their friends!
Hide 10-15 small rolled-up paper scrolls around the playground before kids arrive. Some have parts of Mark 9:23; others have dream clues from Joseph's story.
Split into 2-3 teams. Each team searches for scrolls. When found, read it OUT LOUD boldly before putting it in your bag!
First team to complete the memory verse AND collect 3 dream clues wins!
Materials: Paper scrolls (pre-written), small bags per team. Hide at kid-reachable heights. One adult per team.

outdoor.tip: Help kids connect Joseph's bold speaking to their own lives — we can speak boldly about what God can do, even when we can't see the answer yet!
